The brief gives only the topic ('1,200 notices, 6 reasons, how each was fixed'), so the six reasons and fixes are drawn from standard GST practice (GSTR-2B vs 3B ITC, GSTR-1 vs 3B liability, non-filing incl. nil returns, Rule 37 180-day reversal, Section 17(5)(h) blocked credit for free samples and gifts, e-invoice IRN vs books, IRN cancellable within 24 hours). The founder must confirm each reason against the real 1,200-notice data and may reorder; I deliberately give NO per-reason counts or percentages because none were supplied, and the posts do not claim a ranking. 'Usual cause' lines are general causes, not study findings. Format: 8 posts (hook, six reason posts that each repeat 'GST notice reason N of 6' so a quoted post stands alone, summary + the one link and one action). Posts are separated by 'Post N' labels in this file; those labels are not part of the posts. Checks: whole thread with --genre genre:x_thread; each of the 8 posts separately with --platform plat:x_thread (post lengths 177, 261, 257, 239, 257, 232, 266, 257 weighted characters, link counted as 23).
samples.text:
Post 1
We read all 1,200 GST notices our customers received. Six reasons explain them. Here is each reason and how it was fixed, in plain words for SME owners and accountants. (Thread)

Post 2
GST notice reason 1 of 6: ITC claimed in GSTR-3B is higher than GSTR-2B shows. Usual cause: the supplier filed GSTR-1 late, or the invoice was booked in the wrong month. Fix: match your purchase register to GSTR-2B before every 3B, and claim only what 2B shows.

Post 3
GST notice reason 2 of 6: sales in GSTR-1 do not match the tax paid in GSTR-3B. Usual cause: a credit note or a late invoice reached one return and not the other. Fix: build both returns from the same sales register and compare the two totals before filing.

Post 4
GST notice reason 3 of 6: a return was not filed. This notice arrives even for a month with no sales, because a nil return must also be filed. Fix: one filing calendar with a reminder 5 days before each due date, owned by one named person.

Post 5
GST notice reason 4 of 6: ITC taken on an invoice the buyer has not paid for in 180 days. Rule 37 says that ITC must be reversed, with interest. Fix: run an aged-payables check at day 150, so you pay the supplier or plan the reversal before the notice does.

Post 6
GST notice reason 5 of 6: ITC claimed on goods the law blocks, such as free samples and gifts (Section 17(5)(h)). Fix: tag these purchases as blocked credit when the invoice is entered, so they never reach the ITC figure in your 3B.

Post 7
GST notice reason 6 of 6: e-invoice or e-way bill data differs from what was filed. Usual cause: the invoice was corrected in the books after its IRN was generated. Fix: cancel the IRN within 24 hours; after that, issue a credit note and a fresh invoice. Never edit.

Post 8
The six GST notice reasons: 1 ITC above GSTR-2B, 2 GSTR-1 vs 3B mismatch, 3 missed return, 4 supplier invoices unpaid past 180 days, 5 blocked credit, 6 e-invoice mismatch. The full guide has the fix steps for each, in one checklist: [guide link]

samples.text:
DABBA EXPRESS (डब्बा एक्सप्रेस)
Pitch bible excerpt for the OTT kids-and-family slate. Version 0.1

1. OVERVIEW

Logline: Ten-year-old Tanu discovers that Mumbai's lunchboxes are carried by retired railway robots, and that if three humans learn their secret, the robots will be scrapped.

Format: 8 episodes x 22 minutes. Hindi, with Mumbai Hinglish. Stylised 3D with hand-painted textures. Kids 6-12, co-viewed with family.
Genre: adventure comedy. One lunchbox, one clock, one secret.
Tone comparables: the family warmth of Bluey, the gentle machines of WALL-E, the handmade contraptions of Wallace & Gromit. Mumbai is the setting, not a backdrop.
Central question: how much of a secret is worth keeping when a hungry person is standing in front of you?
Why this slate: every Indian household has a lunchbox story, so a family can watch together and each generation finds its own way in.

2. TONE AND STYLE

Do: warm, funny, punctual. Machines have feelings and are never mocked for being old.
Sample narration: "Mumbai mein ek cheez hamesha waqt par aati hai. Mausam nahi. Dabba."
Don't: villains who threaten harm, or robots that "die". Robots power down and can be recharged.
Sample line we never write: "Isse scrap kar do, kachra hai." Our scrap-cell characters say "File close karni hai."
Language: robots speak formal railway-announcement Hindi ("Gadi sankhya saat, platform shunya par aa rahi hai"). Tanu and her friends speak fast Hinglish. Street characters may use Bambaiya Hindi.
Respect: real dabbawalas are the heroes of this world's history. The robots wear their uniform out of admiration for the system, never to replace it.
Visual references: Mumbai monsoon greys and greens, the black-and-yellow taxis, chawl balconies, brass station fittings.

Sample scene (tone only). INT. CLASSROOM, 12:44. Tanu opens her tiffin and steam rises. Her mother left the house at seven. Outside the window a dabbawala on a bicycle tips his topi at her. His hand clicks, softly, like a switch.
TANU: (whispering) Hello?
The dabbawala freezes. A tiny lamp blinks inside his kurta sleeve.
DABBAWALA: Aapne kuch nahi dekha.
TANU: Maine kuch nahi dekha. Kya tum robot ho?
DABBAWALA: Gadi saat minute late hai.
He pedals away, wobbling, exactly like a tired man.

3. WORLD RULES

Rule 1, Rang-Chinh. Every dabba carries a coloured symbol code on its lid, and the network moves any dabba to any address by that code alone. Cost: a smudged or painted-over code cannot be recovered, and the dabba is "orphaned" at Platform Shunya until its owner is found. Conflict: every monsoon episode starts with a pile of orphans.

Rule 2, Patri Time. Robots run on the old railway timetable and are at full power only when exactly on schedule. Cost: a robot more than five minutes late "stalls" until the next train passes overhead. Conflict: any delay, from rain to a kind detour, puts a crew member at risk.

Rule 3, Local Charge. Robots recharge only by riding a running local train. Cost: a strike, a flooded track or a cancelled train means they slowly dim. Conflict: the finale, when the city's trains stop.

Rule 4, Kurta-Topi Rule. In public every robot must pass as an ordinary dabbawala in white kurta and topi. Cost: in disguise a robot is no faster or stronger than a tired man, and the real gear (long arms, whistle-horn) works only where no human can see. Conflict: every rescue needs a hiding place.

Rule 5, Bhookh Niyam. A robot may never refuse food to a hungry person. Cost: giving away a dabba breaks Rule 1 (the code now has no recipient) and costs minutes under Rule 2. Conflict: kindness against the schedule, the heart of the series.

Rule 6, Teen Ka Taala. The Kabaad Aadesh, the order that retired the robots, stays frozen while fewer than three humans know the secret. At three, the Scrap Cell can reactivate it. Cost: nobody can be told without counting. Conflict: Tanu is human number one, and every curious neighbour is a ticking clock.

Edge cases writers will hit:
A human can carry a dabba but cannot read its Rang-Chinh. Tanu learns the first two symbols in Ep 4, and no other human ever does.
Rule 2 has no excuses. Rain, traffic and kindness all count as late.
A stalled robot cannot charge, so one stall can become three (Rule 3).
Rule 5 covers food only. A robot can say no to money, toys and favours.
Humans who merely suspect do not count toward Rule 6. Humans who are told, or who see a robot without disguise, do.

4. HISTORY

Only events that drive today's stories.

| Year | Event | Why it matters now |
| 1998 | Porter-class robots join Dadar yard | Their rail habits (Rules 2 and 3) never left them |
| 2011 | Kabaad Aadesh orders every robot scrapped | The reason for the secret |
| 2012 | Seeti Kaka hides eleven robots at Platform Shunya as "under repair" | The crew and the network begin |
| Now | Tanu moves to Chembur | Human number one |

5. PLACES

Platform Shunya (प्लेटफ़ॉर्म शून्य). A forgotten platform below Dadar. Looks like a brass-and-green station frozen in 1998; sounds like tin whistles and tiffin lids; smells of hot rotli and machine oil. Controlled by Seeti Kaka. Scenes: the morning sort, orphan rescues, crew arguments.

Sai Niwas, Chembur (साई निवास). Tanu's housing society: a third-floor flat, a stair landing with a shared shoe rack, a rooftop water tank. Smells of tadka at 7 a.m. Controlled by Mrs Bhosle, the society secretary. Scenes: Tanu's lies, family dinners, rooftop meetings.

Wadala Kabaad Yard (वडाला कबाड़ यार्ड). Where the robots should have been melted. Rust, wet iron, crows. Controlled by the Railway Scrap Cell and its auditor Mr Joglekar, who is dry, not cruel. Scenes: infiltration, paperwork comedy, the countdown.

6. FACTIONS

The Dabba Express crew: eleven robots. Goal: stay useful and unseen. Method: the timetable. Resources: the code, the trains. Opposes: the Scrap Cell, politely.
The Railway Scrap Cell: goal: close every open file. Method: audits. Resources: the Aadesh and a stamp. Opposes: the crew, without knowing it exists.
The people of Sai Niwas: goal: lunch on time. Method: gossip. Resources: a very good WhatsApp group. Neutral, and the most dangerous audience.
Relationship map: the crew and the Scrap Cell are opposed; Sai Niwas is neutral to both; Tanu is the only person who stands between all three.

7. CHARACTERS

Tanu Kulkarni (तनु कुलकर्णी), 10.
Want: to find out how her mother's tiffin, packed at 7 a.m., reaches her desk hot at 12:45.
Flaw: she cannot keep a secret when she is excited.
Arc: starts a chatty new kid, ends the one who keeps it.
Voice: "Ruko, ruko, ruko! Mummy toh saat baje nikal jaati hain, phir mera dabba garam kaise aata hai?"
Fixed look: girl, 135 cm, two short braids with yellow ribbons, mustard school pinafore, red canvas backpack with a hand-drawn sun patch.

Seeti Kaka (सीटी काका), the crew leader.
Want: to keep his crew safe by keeping them on time and hidden.
Flaw: he trusts the timetable over people.
Arc: starts rigid, ends late once, on purpose.
Voice: "Dabba kabhi late nahi hota, bitiya. Aur Kaka? Kaka toh ghadi se pehle pahunchta hai."
Fixed look: boxy robot, 190 cm, faded green paint, brass rivets, silver guard's whistle on a chain, white kurta, cream topi.

Signal Didi (सिग्नल दीदी), the dispatcher.
Want: every dabba in the right hand.
Flaw: when a plan fails, she freezes and her lamp stays red.
Arc: starts all plan, ends improvising.
Voice: "Lal matlab ruko, hari matlab chalo, aur peela matlab Tanu, tum kuch chhupa rahi ho."
Fixed look: slim robot, 150 cm, white signal-post body with black bands, round lamp head glowing red, amber or green with her mood, semaphore-flap arms, maroon scarf.

Pahiya (पहिया), the youngest.
Want: to run a route alone.
Flaw: he takes shortcuts.
Arc: starts reckless, ends knowing which shortcut costs too much.
Voice: "Mera route hai, main akela jaunga! Arre... ye rasta kaunsa hai?"
Fixed look: knee-high robot, 70 cm, one big blue rubber wheel with a cargo basket on top, dented orange cap, single round lens eye, a small brass bell.

8. EPISODE ENGINE AND ARCS

Engine: every episode is one dabba against one clock. A dabba arrives at Platform Shunya with a problem (a smudged code, a wrong address, a hungry stranger). The crew has until the lunch bell. One rule exacts its price by the end, and Tanu's help, and her mouth, both rescue the delivery and endanger the secret. Each episode ends on an opened dabba and a human smiling who will never know why.

Season arc: Ep 1, Tanu finds the secret (human one). Eps 2-5, she becomes the crew's unofficial helper while Mr Joglekar's audits close in. Ep 6, her friend Imran sees too much (human two). Ep 8, a monsoon stops every train and the city's lunch depends on the secret. The season ends with human number three, who chooses to help. Season 2 asks what Rule 6 means then.

Sample loglines:
Ep 1, "Garam Dabba": Tanu follows her tiffin underground and meets Seeti Kaka, who has until the lunch bell to get her out and the dabba back on time.
Ep 3, "Bheega Code": rain smudges every lid on the Dadar line, and Signal Didi must read a whole shelf of orphans by heart.
Ep 5, "Bhookha Mehmaan": a hungry stranger asks for a dabba, and Rule 5 collides with Rule 2.
Ep 8, "Local Band": a flood stops the trains, the crew runs low on charge, and the only help left is human.

9. GLOSSARY

dabba (डब्बा): lunchbox. DUB-baa.
dabbawala (डब्बावाला): a real Mumbai lunchbox carrier. DUB-baa-waa-laa.
Platform Shunya (प्लेटफ़ॉर्म शून्य): the hidden base. platform SHOON-yaa.
Rang-Chinh (रंग-चिह्न): the lid code. rung-CHIN-h.
Patri Time (पटरी टाइम): timetable power. PUT-ree time.
Local Charge (लोकल चार्ज): recharging on a running train.
Kurta-Topi Rule (कुर्ता-टोपी नियम): the disguise rule. KUR-taa TOE-pee.
Bhookh Niyam (भूख नियम): the hunger rule. bhookh NI-yum.
Kabaad Aadesh (कबाड़ आदेश): the scrap order. kuh-BAAD aa-DAYSH.
Teen Ka Taala (तीन का ताला): the three-human lock. TEEN kaa TAA-laa.
